Sports.title: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg stripped of Marseille captaincy after rejecting Premier League switch
Sports.content:
Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has reportedly been removed as Marseille's captain after rejecting a £15million transfer to Newcastle last week.

Hojbjerg played 90 minutes for the French side against Atletico Madrid on Friday, but he did so without the armband.



3 Hojbjerg (left) has lost the captain's armband for Marseille after rejecting Newcastle Credit: AFP

French news outlet RMC Sport claim the Danish midfielder has been punished by club chiefs for angering them with his decision.

Newcastle approached Marseille to try and sign Hojbjerg as a potential replacement for Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies wanted some extra experience added to the squad after losing their captain to Arsenal for £75m.



However, Hojbjerg turned down the chance to return to the Premier League in a deal that was set to be worth £15m.

That would have frustrated Newcastle, but it has also left Marseille angry, with owner Frank McCourt alleged to be fuming.



And so much so, McCourt and the Ligue 1 side's management are said to have opted to strip their midfielder of captaincy, handing it to Timothy Weah instead.

They reportedly wanted the transfer to happen to bring in some much-needed funds and reduce their wage bill.



The club want individual interests to take a back seat to overall interests - so to prove that stance, they have punished Hojbjerg.

Could Hojbjerg still leave Marseille?

Hojbjerg's full involvement in Marseille's friendly on Friday, despite not being captain, indicated he could still stay at the club.

But there is still interest from other teams in Europe, including Serie A giants AC Milan, according to reports in Italy.

3 Hojbjerg angered Marseille chiefs by turning down a return to England Credit: Getty Images - Getty



Ruben Amorim could be looking to add some new faces to his squad amid a refresh of players following his appointment.

Amorim has recently put Fikayo Tomori, Christopher Nkunku and Youssouf Fofana up for sale.

Should any of those players leave, particularly midfielder Fofana, Milan could potentially make a move for Hojbjerg.

Hojbjerg labelled 'incredibly average'

Hojbjerg has played 254 Premier League games throughout his career, starring for Tottenham and Southampton.



But the 31-year-old opted not to make a move back to England, leaving Newcastle having to look at other options.

However, talkSPORT's Jeff Stelling doesn't think the Magpies missed out on much by the Dane rejecting them.

3 Stelling thinks Newcastle haven't missed out on much by Hojbjerg not joining Credit: Getty

"I know they wanted experience, he's 31 and he's done well at Marseille," Stelling said on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"But his last season at Tottenham, he made eight Premier League starts and didn't play successive Premier League games at all.

"I think he's incredibly average."

Last season, Hojbjerg played 43 games for Marseille, scoring five goals and assisting another five.

But his future at the club remains in doubt, particularly now that he has lost the captain's armband.

Sports.title: WEST HAM FAN VIEW: The Championship could be a perfect reset button, but with a lack new blood and nagging ownership doubts we know how quickly things can go wrong...
Sports.content:
West Ham fans braced themselves for the worst following relegation from the Premier League in May.

Justified pessimism, you would think, after a season in which they won ten games, drew nine and lost 19.

The star players will soon be gone and so perhaps the financial burden and emotional turmoil of being a West Ham season ticket holder would be hard to justify.

And yet, instead of desperation and despair, there has been an unprecedented sense of unity with fans, players, owners all rallying around the club.

There is even a feeling that a season in the Championship could be the reset the club needs and could act as a catalyst for long-term change.

However, West Ham fans like myself know full well that things can soon take a turn for the worse…

Nuno Espirito Santo is pictured on the day West Ham were relegated - he remains in charge

Ownership, or one-upmanship?

The most significant change has been at the top with Karren Brady and latterly David Sullivan stepping down.

The Czech billionaire and Royal Mail owner, Daniel Kretinsky, is both director and major shareholder of the club. Kretinsky helped generate hope and optimism as he took steps to retain two of West Ham’s key components ‑ their talisman and their manager.

Skipper Jarrod Bowen said of his decisive meeting with Kretinsky: ‘I flew out to Prague in the Czech Republic to meet Daniel and Jiri (Svarc, his right hand man) and the ambition that I got from them, certainly in terms of the direction the club wants to move in, it interests me a lot.’ He stayed.

Similarly, while many West Ham fans thought Nuno’s departure was a foregone conclusion and something that Sullivan had pushed for, Kretinsky placed significant emphasis on persuading him to stay.

Nuno remaining is vital for West Ham. Having a Premier League-calibre manager, who helped to get Wolves promoted with 99 points in 2018, provides much needed stability at the London Stadium.

West Ham United owner Daniel Kretinsky (centre) helped to generate some optimism

Everything seemed to be looking stable and there was a clear connection between the board and the club. However, West Ham would not be West Ham if there wasn’t some turmoil at the top.

On August 1, Vanessa Gold, daughter of the late West Ham co-owner, David Gold, announced that she planned to sell the family shares to a consortium led by ex-Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

What followed was a frenzy of back-and-forth, with loaded statements by Kretinsky, saying: ‘The agreement with the Gold family provided stability at crucial time. This does the opposite.’

Whether this Succession-style conflict will spell trouble for the Hammers is unclear, but the reshuffling behind the club is coming at the wrong time, as West Ham begin their Championship season at Burnley on Sunday.

Fan power

It is thought that the departures of Sullivan and Brady, combined with Kretinsky’s promising start, played a huge role in the rush to buy season tickets. West Ham announced that over 50,000 season tickets had been sold, a figure that dwarfs previous Championship attendance records and shows a set of resilient fans backing their team.

There were glimpses of this connection last season, especially when West Ham won three consecutive home Premier League games, a feat they had not achieved since March 2019.

Fans are treating this season as a restart and a new era away from the clutches of Brady and Sullivan, no VAR, two fixtures against Millwall and an opportunity to win plenty of games.

There was also a growing expectation that in the Championship the club would draw on the fabled Academy that has produced down the years stars like Bobby Moore, Rio Ferdinand, Frank Lampard and Joe Cole.

Freddie Potts is one of a number of young players at the club to have moved on

Surely players like George Earthy, Callum Marshall and Freddie Potts could use their experience in the EFL to provide cost-effective options in West Ham’s promotion push.

However, Marshall has joined League One Luton Town and Potts left for Club Brugge for £10million. Potts' departure stings the most as fans believed his experience on loan in the Championship at Wycombe and Portsmouth would have been invaluable.

Former great Kevin Nolan, who scored 31 goals in 157 appearances for the Irons, expressed his concern.

‘I think this probably could turn out to be a bit of a mistake, but it's good money for Freddie,’ Nolan said. ‘I thought that he could be one of the players who could stand up this year for West Ham.’

This sentiment is echoed by former Hammers striker Tony Cottee, who says: ‘I don't get it…I played with his dad (Steve), and I want to see the Academy players.’

The loss of academy players could yet see the good faith that Kretinsky built up to begin to ebb away.

Ins and outs

This faith was never at a higher level than on July 17 when Bowen announced he was committing to another season. ‘We're going to need a real tight knit, a real togetherness, a real understanding of what we want from each other,’ the forward said.

This sense of togetherness and commitment seems to be echoing around the locker room where the Hammers have been able to keep their core group intact ‑ with only two big-name departures confirmed.

Midfielder Mateus Fernandes joined London rivals Tottenham for an eye-watering £85m, almost £50m more than West Ham paid Southampton for him a year earlier.

Winger Crysencio Summerville joined Al Hilal for £60m, a good mark-up again after arriving from Leeds for £25m only two seasons ago and scoring just six goals in 50 appearances for West Ham.

Both departures were seen as inevitable but gaining close to £150m for the duo was seen as a shrewd bit of business.

Jarrod Bowen chose to stay with the Hammers in a huge boost to promotion chances

There were fears that Dinos Mavropanos, a man reborn last season, and newcomer Taty Castellanos would follow the pair out the door. However, both seem committed to the club and prepared to fight for promotion next season, another reason for optimism.

On the down side, the club have been quiet in the transfer market except for signings of Keiber Lamadrid and Joel Veltman.

In midfield, we have an ageing James Ward-Prowse, an injured Tomas Soucek, the inconsistent Soungoutou Magassa and an unproven Mohamadou Kanté.

West Ham’s relegation to the Championship led to restructuring at each level of the club, a renewed connection between the club and its fans and stability in all the right places.

However, recent developments around ownership and a backtrack on youth policy seem to have set them back. The jury is out.

Sports.title: The season hasn't even started but Arsenal already look way ahead of the chasing pack. Their rivals, shrouded in uncertainty, have stood still this summer, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
The curtain will rise at the Principality Stadium on Sunday afternoon and the champions will walk out on to the stage ahead of the Community Shield. Arsenal’s cast will not look radically different. There will be a few extras and one or two new stars but nothing dramatic. There has been no need for drama. Just steady growth.

Arsenal did not need to have a spectacular summer in the transfer market. It was important that they strengthened from a position of strength and they have started that process calmly by recruiting Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle. With two weeks of the window remaining, there is an argument that it is the best signing of the close season so far.

Other arrivals are being discussed. The champions need reinforcements in defence where long-term injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber are a concern and have led to an as-yet fruitless pursuit of Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

Arsenal are said to be interested in Jarell Quansah, at Bayer Leverkusen. They have spoken about prolific striker Victor Osimhen from Galatasaray and hope they can lure Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid.

If they add more quality in the next fortnight to supplement the signings of Guimaraes and Greece forward Christos Tzolis, then it will probably be enough to put them out of reach of the rest for another year.

They are already strong favourites with the bookmakers to retain the title they won by seven points from Manchester City last season. They have a solid look, just as they did last season, when solidity got them over the line.

Arsenal and Man City go head-to-head once more in the Community Shield on Sunday

The Gunners have strengthened from a position of strength and new signing Bruno Guimaraes will likely be involved

They are the favourites because of their own virtues, because of the depth and the quality of their squad and because, now they have ended a title drought that lasted for more than 20 years, much of the pressure that impeded them in the second half of last season will have fallen from their shoulders.

But they are also favourites because uncertainty shrouds their rivals. They are favourites because City have lost manager Pep Guardiola and the rest have not done enough to close the gap.

Manchester United looked like the coming club at the end of last season but an underwhelming summer in the transfer market so far has led many to question whether they can take the great leap forward they would need to unseat the champions. It feels as if their momentum has stalled.

City, Arsenal’s opponents in Cardiff, pushed Arteta’s side close last season but since then, they have lost Guardiola, one of the greatest managers English football has ever seen, and they are struggling to keep hold of the man many still see as their best player, Rodri.

It remains to be seen whether Guardiola’s replacement, Enzo Maresca, can handle the pressure of following Guardiola and the increased demands he will face at a club like City that is used to winning.

Maresca considered it such a great achievement finishing fourth with Chelsea in 2024-25 that he was emboldened enough to tell the club’s critics to ‘F Off’. Finish fourth with City and he may find himself booted out on to the east Manchester pavement.

Andoni Iraola is widely seen as a progressive managerial appointment for Liverpool but their defence of their title under Arne Slot last season was so disappointing that it may be too much to expect them to bridge the gap to Arsenal.

They have been linked consistently with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola but even if they sign him, is that an improvement on Mohamed Salah? Much will depend on whether we see the real Florian Wirtz during this campaign.

Arsenal are favourites to win another Premier League title because of their quality and depth

It is yet to be seen whether Man City boss Enzo Maresca can handle the pressure of following Pep Guardiola

Amid that blaze of uncertainty, Arsenal are operating with the closest thing to certainty in the league. Everything about them says they are trading up. Leandro Trossard was an important player for them last season and Gabriel Martinelli scored goals, too, but Trossard has gone and Martinelli’s future is uncertain.

As Arsenal try to reach higher, they are identifying areas where they can improve and acting with requisite ruthlessness. Tzolis is seen as an upgrade on Trossard and Martinelli, if Osimhen arrives, he will be seen as an upgrade on Viktor Gyokeres. Guimaraes, wherever he fits into midfield, is proven quality.

And then there is Max Dowman. Until now, Dowman has been seen as a wonderkid, a startlingly brilliant and precocious teenager, a tantalising curiosity rather than a title game-changer. Dowman is still only 16 but he is so good and so exciting that his progress signifies another reason why Arsenal should be stronger this season than they were last year.

Many believe he has the kind of talent that justifies him being mentioned in the same bracket as Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. His development means Arsenal will get the equivalent of a new superstar signing every season for the next couple of years.

There is still time for others to make inroads into the advantages Arsenal hold over them but there has been a studied maturity about the champions’ summer that carries a sense of foreboding for the rest. When the curtain rises in Cardiff, their lead over the rest will not have diminished since the end of last season. It will have grown.

Sports.title: Horrifying pictures emerge in aftermath of Finlay Tarling's fatal crash as report suggests car was travelling on the correct side of the road despite previous claims
Sports.content:
Fresh questions have emerged over the death of British cyclist Finlay Tarling after a Portuguese journalist disputed initial reports that the car involved in the fatal collision was travelling on the wrong side of the road.

The 19-year-old Welsh rider, who had raced for Great Britain on the road and track, died during the Volta a Portugal on Friday.

Posting on social media, Portuguese cycling commentator Paulo Martins shared pictures of the damaged white van which appeared to show the collision with the windscreen, and Tarling's shattered bike.

In the caption he wrote: 'Initial reports indicated the vehicle was driving on the wrong side of the road, but images seen on various TV channels show that the car was going in the right direction.

'For this reason, I feel obligated to clarify what I had written incorrectly, as these were news reports that had been given by various TV channels in Portugal.

'Now it's a matter of understanding how that vehicle ended up in that location.

'Was it authorized to continue its journey by the police? Did it break through the security cordon?

'Nothing will bring this boy back to the world of the living, and may everyone in the future respect human life, because there is a brother, a son, a father, friends, girlfriend or wife who will suffer immensely, and I have no doubt that the driver himself, even if he may not be at fault, will also be scarred for the rest of his life.'

The 19-year-old Welsh rider (second from left), who had raced for Great Britain on the road and track, died during the Volta a Portugal on Friday

Terribili le immagini della scena dell'incidente e della bici accartocciata del povero Tarling, via @RTPNoticias #ciclismo pic.twitter.com/rLkcDkmV3U — Stefano Rizzato (@stefanorizzato) August 14, 2026

Tarling was on the eighth stage of the race when the incident occurred on a 166.8km route to Fafe, in the north of the country.

In a statement provided to local media, Major Tiago Machado of the National Republican Guard said there had been 'a collision between the cyclist and a light goods vehicle' and that an investigation was under way.

According to Portuguese media Tarling was given immediate medical attention but died shortly after the crash. The race was neutralised about 20km from the finish line.

Tarling's team NSN said in a statement: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

'Fin was a much-loved member of our team but, most importantly, he was a son, a brother and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

'Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents, Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend.'

Tarling's older brother Josh is a world champion cyclist on the track and a stage winner at last year's Giro d'Italia. Josh made his Olympic debut at Paris 2024, where he came fourth in the men's time trial.

Portugal's President, Antonio Jose Seguro, said Tarling's death 'saddens the peloton, the race, and the country that welcomed him'.

He offered his 'deepest condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates at NSN Development Team, and to the entire cycling community, joining in their grief with deep emotion'.

A statement from world governing body the UCI read: 'The UCI is deeply saddened by the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling, who passed away following a serious accident during today's eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

'The UCI extends its deepest condolences to Finlay's family, friends and team-mates.'

Tarling looked to be following in the footsteps of his older brother Josh - who made his Olympic debut at Paris 2024 - as a time trial specialist

Meanwhile, the sport's governing body in Wales added: 'We at Beicio Cymru (Welsh Cycling) are absolutely devastated to hear the news of Fin Tarling's passing today while competing at the Volta in Portugal.

'Fin was an incredible athlete, role model, friend, brother and son. We send our love and deepest condolences to Mike, Dawn and Josh at this incredibly difficult time.

'Rest in peace, Fin. You were incredible, and we will always remember you.'

The Volta a Portugal got under way in Lisbon on 5 August and is raced over 10 stages, concluding in Porto on 16 August.

Tarling looked to be following in the footsteps of his older brother Josh as a time trial specialist.

He finished in third in the under-23 men's individual time trial at the British Championships in June and competed in the Tour of Britain just under 12 months ago.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace complete £21m signing of full back Anan Khalaili, while Southampton reject Benfica's opening bid for Harwood-Bellis: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Benfica offer for Harwood-Bellis rejected

Southampton have rejected a £17.5million offer from Benfica for defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Portuguese side, coached by Marco Silva, turned to the 24-year-old after initial interest in Chelsea's Tosin Adarabioyo who wants to stay at Stamford Bridge.

Benfica are considering an improved offer with Harwood-Bellis interested in the move.

Benfica are considering an improved offer for Saints' Harwood-Bellis after having their initial bid of £17.5million rejected, while the 24-year-old is interested in the move

Forest sign Benda

Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of former Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda.

The 27-year-old is being brought in to replace the departed Angus Gunn as third-choice. He had spells on loan at Feyenoord and Millwall last season.

Eagles sign £21m right back Khalaili

Crystal Palace have completed the £21million signing of Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili.

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend.

The 21-year-old is being brought in to provide competition for Daniel Munoz at right wing-back.

However, there is no guarantee that the £20m-rated Colombian will stay beyond this summer amid interest from the likes of Tottenham and Everton. He has two years left on his deal.

Khalaili, who has won 16 caps for Israel, said: 'I'm happy to be here, I'm excited, and I can't wait to start.

'I’ve followed the Premier League. It's a new challenge for me, and I've followed Crystal Palace for a long time. I'm happy to be here.'

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend

Gourna-Douath 'excited' to join Tigers

Hull City have finalised the £3.5m transfer of French defensive midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath from RB Salzburg.

The deal is worth £2.9m guaranteed, plus add-ons and a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

The 23-year-old has signed a five-year contract, becoming the club’s 10th summer signing.

Gourna-Douath said: 'I’m really happy because it was such a long journey from the first phone call until I signed. I’m so excited to get started.

'I’m really happy to have this experience. I got a chance to play in the Champions League, Serie A and Ligue 1.

'I've learned a lot and I’m really happy to put this experience on the pitch in the Premier League. The Premier League is the dream of all footballers. Now, I have a chance to play in the Premier League, so I am excited to play.'

Sports.title: Golden girl Keely Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as British star loses her 800m European Championship crown with second-place finish - with Olympic champion jokingly removing her medal in disappointed post-race interview
Sports.content:
Audrey Werro is fast becoming an unsolvable riddle for the leading lady of British sport. For the second time in 10 weeks, this Swiss phenomenon left Keely Hodgkinson staring at her heels in a race that lived up to its billing as the best of the European Championships.

To the most talented Audrey since Hepburn went the 800m gold medal. To Hodgkinson, there was presumably no silver lining to be found in finishing a close second on home soil.

If there is to be any consolation, it is that Werro, aged 22, clocked a championship record of 1:54.81 on a chilly, breezy evening in Birmingham to beat her. But warmer thoughts will be harder to find for Hodgkinson.

Instead, the Olympic champion must process the dawning of a serious rivalry and one that is not currently swinging in her favour. This one was settled by the margin of 0.2sec.

In the long run, Hodgkinson might view such moments as the competitive nectar needed for the breaching of new frontiers, of course, but the sting in the present will be real. Not many athletes have the finishing speed to match Hodgkinson, but in their past two races Werro has kicked away from her with the force of a donkey.

The decisive move here came after 500 metres, when Werro put the hammer down.

Hodgkinson, who had been near enough level at the bell after a 56sec opening lap, went with her, and they both separated from Femke Broeders-Bol in third, but the Brit had no answer. She never got her nose in front, and those moments of futility can leave lasting doubts in an athlete.

The 24-year-old, who was chasing a third straight European title, was evidently in little mood to indulge the celebrations of on-track interviewer Iwan Thomas. He assumed she would be thrilled with silver, but Hodgkinson responded: ‘I think I would be happier with a gold.’

Kely Hodgkinson was forced to settle for second in the women's 800m final on Friday

Hodgkinson jokingly took off her silver medal at the European Championships in Birmingham

She later added: ‘I think with that level of competition, any medal is a really good achievement and another one to add to my collection so I can never be disappointed with that. But I'm defending champion so I wanted to do that.

‘I knew it was going to come down to the wire but I really thought I was going to win today. But it wasn't meant to be. I didn't do anything wrong, it was just one of those things.

‘Congrats to Audrey. I am sure we will have more battles.’

That much seems certain. And for two women striving to break the oldest world record in track athletics, that will be a good thing.

But Werro has the edge. Having been beaten twice by Hodgkinson during the indoor portion of the season, she gained spectacular revenge in Stockholm in June when the Brit set a personal best of 1:54.33. Not only was that a win against a full-form Hodgkinson, Werro’s time of 1:53.98 was the third quickest in history. A month later, Werro ran quicker again with a 1:53.80 – if anyone is to better the dubious mark of 1:53.28 set by the Czech Jarmila Kratochvilova in the Eighties, Werro might have the edge.

To think, Werro was only cleared to race in this final on appeal after being tripped in her semi-final. It was a marginal call but also the correct one, so there should be no controversy around what it led to.

For Hodgkinson, the bigger picture will make for strange viewing. After the injury troubles of 2025, her times in 2026 have moved sharply on an upward trajectory, including the indoor world record in February, so she rightly resents any suggestion of ‘failure’ at losing a race or two. She was borderline tetchy in using that label prior to these Championships.

But in athletics, the clock is a secondary adversary to the field and Werro’s emergence is a huge fly in the ointment. For the rest of us watching, we can presumably take great pleasure in where it leads, because athletics needs rivalries. In these two gifted runners, it has one that has the potential to go on for years.

Sports.title: MMA star Ian Machado Garry eyes more than an upset at UFC 330 amid promoter Eddie Hearn's bitter rivalry with Dana White
Sports.content:
Top UFC welterweight Ian Machado Garry could be fighting for more than a triumph in the octagon on Saturday night.

After signing with Matchroom Chairman Eddie Hearn - the bitter rival to UFC and ZUFFA Boxing frontman Dana White - Garry, 28, is set to face off against two-division UFC champion Islam Makhachev this weekend.

And, should Garry pull off the major upset in UFC 330’s main event, it could mark more than achievement for the fighter alone.

A potential victory will see English promoter Hearn have two UFC champions in his stable of athletes - something that would certainly irk UFC brass.

Hearn previously signed UFC heavyweight champion, Tom Aspinall, 33, as a counter move to White stealing away longtime Matchroom athlete, Conor Benn, 29.

Benn got his feet wet by winning his first ZUFFA Boxing fight against Regis Prograis back in April and now has a massive fight lined up against polarizing boxing superstar, Ryan Garcia, 28, on September 12.

Top UFC welterweight Ian Machado Garry is set to enter the octagon on Saturday night

Garry is set to face off against two-division UFC champion Islam Makhachev at UFC 330

Now, it's Garry’s turn to bolster Hearn’s revenge. If Garry beats Makhachev tomorrow, it would soothe much of the pain the Matchroom chief felt when he lost Benn to White earlier this year.

It would also give Hearn some momentum towards finally booking a Ciryl Gane and Tom Aspinall rematch – a fight that could be set amongst the scenic views of the Eiffel Tower in Paris.

Garry understands on many levels what a win over the current world’s pound-for-pound number one fighter would do not only for his career, but also for the growth of his brand in the Europe market which is controlled and operated by Hearn and his sports agency team.

‘For me, it was an absolute no-brainer,’ the Irish fighter said of the partnership. ‘As someone who grew up in Ireland and is living in England right now, when you talk about the biggest sports promoter in our region, it is Eddie Hearn, it is Matchroom, and they've been successful at it for God knows how long at this point.’

When it comes to working with Hearn it’s more than just about money and opportunity for Garry, it’s about respecting the person you are conducting business with.

‘I love [the Hearn’s] family bond. I love Eddie's relationship with his dad. I love how they work. We've known their team for a while,’ he said.

Garry can’t deny Matchroom’s generational success, and the effect they’ve had on the European market.

‘[Signing with Matchroom] was the right decision at the right time to help grow my brand, grow my name and do it together so that we can bring more eyes to all of my fights,’ he added. ‘We can bring more attention to when I compete and that's my focus.’

The Irish fighter is signed with Matchroom Chairman Eddie Hearn's agency

UFC 330 will take place inside the Xinity Arena located in the heart of Rocky’s hometown - Philadelphia.

Garry is facing a swift and technical champion in Dagestan’s Makhachev - a longtime teammate of all-time great fighter Khabib Nurmagomedov.

For Makhachev, after moving up from the lightweight division, the New Jersey-living grappling phenom and all-time great is attempting to achieve UFC history by winning 17-straight fights inside of the octagon for his first title defense at 170-pounds.

Both men aim to outthink and outwill the other in what has the makings to be one of the most competitive fights of the year, even though Garry is a major underdog despite his incredible performances over the division's two bogeymen, Carlos Prates and Shavkat Rakhmonov.

Will Garry get the upset and become the newly crowned champ or will Makhachev have his way with the elusive striker and enforce his vice grip squeeze?

Hearn will likely be saying an extra prayer for his guy to shock the world and swipe out one of White’s bishops.

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca has already stamped his mark on Man City: New training methods, new leaders, new build-up play, new demands on his goalkeepers... same sky-high expectations as Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
The Manchester City dressing room has looked within itself this summer, wondering about hangovers and resets and their changing world. The king is dead and all that.

Expectation is a theme that some have explored privately, asking themselves what ought to be considered reasonable. Even in the final two seasons, with Pep Guardiola’s side on the wane and then at the beginning of a rebuild that shifted their tactical ideals, they managed to secure Champions League qualification and won both domestic cup competitions, running Arsenal to the last week of the title race too.

Same again please, Enzo Maresca. Apparently, this is the norm.

‘It’s not the change (itself) that worried me,’ said Matheus Nunes. ‘Even ourselves as players, you have to remember what the club has done. When you think about it, it is almost impossible to win six Premier Leagues in 10 years. This is not normal and people forget that.

‘Sometimes you have to go through a year or two of not winning to get to the win. Maybe it will be different (for us), who knows? Maybe it won’t. The club deserves us to try.’

It sounds as if City’s squad are heading into this new dawn with their eyes wide open, with a realisation of what can happen – and what has happened very close by in the not-too-distant past – once a patriarch slowly raises the hand. This is an unknown. An exciting unknown, an unknown that provokes intrigue, starting on Sunday for the Community Shield with Arsenal in Cardiff.

Enzo Maresca's arrival is an unknown. An exciting unknown, an unknown that provokes intrigue

The Italian knows as well as anyone what the expectation levels are at Manchester City, having been on Pep Guardiola's staff for the Treble-winning campaign

The Shield is a piece of silverware that the coaches all count towards their various hauls, and Maresca is no different, but one that ultimately does not hold a great deal of weight.

Those who have been with the new manager during pre-season appeared ready for competitive action when beating Atletico Madrid 3-1 in Seoul last weekend, showcasing the sort of verve in the final third that the Italian has been preaching during hour-long sessions in the searing heat. He has been encouraged by steadily improving displays, believing it is vindicating the ideas being imparted during training.

They had been struggling to breathe in South Korea days earlier during a friendly against the K-League All Stars. Staff members remarked between themselves afterwards that half the team could barely cope with the heat, officially 40°C but feeling like 45.

Josko Gvardiol had to be propped up by a team-mate at one point before going down on his haunches. Staff watching from the stands kept cool with a handheld electric fan in each hand. Merely attending was sweat inducing, let alone playing.

There will be a school of thought that those conditions can accelerate fitness regimes and proof of that or otherwise will soon become evident. Maresca had to be creative with the timings of his sessions so as to best avoid the real extremities, wrestling with either early morning or evening starts at the Mokdong Stadium – lacking shade, home to second division football and, somewhat ironically, often an ice rink.

The winters are cold in that part of the world but much the opposite problem here, with Maresca plumping for 7pm training over 9am. The rationale was that players sleep so poorly in Asia due to the time difference that mornings were effectively redundant anyway. In the end, the difference in temperature appeared negligible.

To illustrate the obsession of the man now leading City, and who probably evokes memories of his predecessor, a thought popped into the head of Maresca before a training session open to the public in Hong Kong.

They would be running through how to press Inter in a friendly 24 hours later, working on team shape as he attempted to quickly implement his ideas. The idea that the opposition could be watching and taking notes did briefly percolate. That was until he realised that none of it matters.

Staff members remarked after a friendly against the K-League All Stars in Seoul that half the team could barely cope with the heat, officially 40°C but feeling like 45

Maresca opted for evening training sessions as players sleep so poorly in Asia due to the time difference that mornings were effectively redundant anyway

City’s red-eye arrived home on Monday morning and it has been a long wait for Maresca to welcome the entire squad back, with six only returning this week from the World Cup.

One of them, Rodri, is expected to be the most high-profile departure over the coming weeks and the City manager needs to reshape his leadership quartet, with only Ruben Dias and Erling Haaland left from last year.

They head for the Principality Stadium with questions over the make-up of the squad and how much change will take hold before the transfer window (or ‘window transfer’, as Maresca endearingly calls it) shuts. Uncertainty lingers as to how many go and how many join.

In that sense, the Maresca era beginning off the back of a major international tournament is not perfect, given that transfers are pushed back until after mandatory breaks.

The lone major signing so far, £116million Elliot Anderson, would fit the mould of this City or the last one, though, which points to a more seamless transition than perhaps occurs elsewhere.

‘When you change a manager and go for a new one, it’s good to go for a manager with a similar idea,’ Maresca said. ‘That way, with the players you have and the players you recruited, they more or less have the same style. Like with the Elliot one, even though I was not here, he still fits in.’

Players are describing the ideas as similar but different. They will defend differently, for starters. There will be less tactical tinkering, more wedded to the principal concept. ‘What he wants is really clear,’ said Nico Gonzalez. ‘The structure is really clear.’

If Anderson fits effortlessly, work is going on behind the scenes to make sure Gianluigi Donnarumma does as well, now wearing the No1 shirt after James Trafford’s move to Leeds United. Distribution is not the finest part of his game and City are looking at solutions to help their goalkeeper contribute on the ball and not ask for anything overly elaborate.

The lone major signing so far, £116million Elliot Anderson, would fit the mould of this City or the last one, though, which points to a more seamless transition than perhaps occurs elsewhere

Gianluigi Donnarumma has been doing extra work at the end of sessions with coaches Richard Wright and Michele De Bernardin, relentlessly clipping 30 or 40-yard balls towards wide areas

The real stuff begins on Sunday and Maresca has no time to waste. For him, silverware is silverware

One of those ideas is to build up with three defenders rather than two, giving more security for possible mistakes and more options when passing.

Donnarumma has been doing extra work at the end of sessions with coaches Richard Wright and Michele De Bernardin, relentlessly clipping 30 or 40-yard balls towards wide areas. Maresca had his head in his hands when one simple pass was given straight to Atletico inside City’s own third on Sunday. Typically, Donnarumma bailed himself out.

Extra sessions were part of Maresca’s remit when he was assistant to Guardiola during the Treble campaign. Notably he worked on specifics with Rico Lewis and Phil Foden and the latter is partial to games with the manager after sessions have ended now.

‘From the first week, the messaging was very direct, very honest,’ Lewis said. It needs to be. The real stuff begins on Sunday and Maresca has no time to waste. For him, silverware is silverware.

Sports.title: Zharnel Hughes could be upgraded to 200m gold over winner's 'missed doping test'
Sports.content:
Zharnel Hughes could be upgraded to 200m gold over winner's 'missed doping test'

Britain's Zharnel Hughes took home a silver medal in the 200m final at the European Athletics Championships on Friday night, but there are question marks over winner Owen Ansah

View 2 Images Owen Ansah won 200m gold ahead of Zharnel Hughes (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Owen Ansah won the gold medal in the final of the men's 200m at the European Athletics Championships on Friday night, despite facing a potential ban over allegedly failing to comply with a doping test.

‌



The German ran 19.95 to beat Britain's Zharnel Hughes to the finish line at the Alexander Stadium in Birmingham. Hughes held the lead coming into the home straight but was reeled in by the 25-year-old.

‌



Yet Ansah's moment of glory came with a significant asterisk following a statement from the National Anti Doping Agency of Germany (NADA) last week, which said he had refused or failed to submit to sample collection. NADA have called for a four-year ban for the sprinter, but he was free to compete in Birmingham because there was no immediate suspension.

‌



Ansah disputes the alleged violation. He has previously explained that an anti-doping official arrived at his house to conduct an out-of-competition test as he was leaving for Monaco. Ansah said he therefore couldn't provide a urine sample and explained that he wasn't aware of the potential consequences.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Keely Hodgkinson takes off medal during live BBC interview after crushing defeat READ MORE :

Amy Hunt wins European 200m gold at Birmingham 2026 READ MORE :

NADA has given him 20 days to respond to the findings or “or request the initiation of disciplinary proceedings before the German Court of Arbitration for Sport.” If the four-year ban ends up standing then Ansah will be stripped of his medals from Birmingham, which also include a bronze in the 100m, with the athletes below him promoted.

‌



"I hope everyone will know my name now," Ansah said after his win on Friday night. "This was the goal – to leave the Europeans with two medals, a bronze and gold is amazing for me.

"The stadium is crazy today. Before the race, I was told that the stadium was sold out and I wanted to give Birmingham a show. I did it.

View 2 Images Owen Ansah is under investigation for allegedly missing a drugs test (Image: Sam Mellish/Getty Images)

‌



"The 100m bronze was just a warm up for me. The 200m was always the main goal. My coach always told me I am a 200m sprinter. Today I finally believed it."

Hughes had mixed feelings after the race. "I have had a very up and down season," he said. "I have had very issues with my body which means I have had to make some adaptions throughout the season.

"But I dug deep, refocused and knew I really wanted to come here and make a good effort, which was hard as I was exhausted mentally more than physically. I have to keep believing in myself and that is what I did."

Article continues below

He added: "Today's race was a good one. I felt good and came round the bend with so much speed I thought I was out of control. I did my best to navigate it as best as I could and control the lactic. But suddenly Ansah was away from me 20 metres from the end. It sucks but I gave my all.

"I am pleased to add silver to my European collection and I am here to get more. I am looking forward to joining the guys now and focusing for the relay."

Sports.title: Victor Osimhen breaks silence on Arsenal transfer rumours after £58m talks
Sports.content:
Victor Osimhen breaks silence on Arsenal transfer rumours after £58m talks

Victor Osimhen is dominating transfer headlines yet again, with Arsenal being identified as a possible destination for the Galatasaray forward

View 3 Images Victor Osimhen could be set for a move to the Premier League with Arsenal interested in the striker (Image: Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)

Arsenal transfer target Victor Osimhen offered a 'wait and see' style response to speculation linking him to the Emirates Stadium. As is the case during nearly every transfer window, the Nigerian is being linked to the Premier League again.

‌



Having regularly been mentioned in the same breath as Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are now the two clubs believed to be interested. His name was brought up when the Gunners were in transfer talks with Galatasaray, who were looking to secure a move for Ethan Nwaneri and Gabriel Martinelli.

‌



While Martinelli rejected a move to Istanbul, Osimhen appeared to keep his options open when the rumours linking him to Arsenal were put to him. While stopping short of ruling out a departure from Galatasaray, he was equally keen to stress his mind is firmly fixed on pre-season preparations, with Arsenal said to be considering a move for the £58m-rated forward.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: "There are always rumours in transfer seasons. I will take care of my business. I am focused on my job, then we will see and think further."

Back in 2023, Osimhen made no secret of his ambition to one day play in the Premier League, at a time when he was in stunning form for Napoli as they stormed to the Serie A title.

‌



"I think playing in one of the top five leagues in the world is an amazing feeling for me," he said after being named 'Best Foreign Athlete of the Year' by the Italian Foreign Press Association in 2023.

View 3 Images Osimhen's future is uncertain (Image: Ferda Demir, Getty Images)

"A lot of people worldwide consider the Premier League as the best and the strongest league but now I'm in one of the best leagues in the world which is the Italian Serie A.

‌



"I'm working so hard to make sure that I achieve my dream of playing in the Premier League some day but like I said, it's a process and I just want to keep on this momentum and continue to do well."

Currently, Arsenal have Viktor Gyokeres spearheading the attack, with Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also on hand as centre-forward alternatives. Defensive midfielder Mikel Merino has also demonstrated a talent for finding the net when utilised as a striker by Arteta previously.

View 3 Images Arteta and Arsenal are chasing back-to-back titles (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal have also been connected with a potential swoop for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, though the Spanish giants are said to be holding out for upwards of £100m for the Argentinian. The Gunners have encountered considerable disappointment regarding their striking targets this summer.

They have already seen attempts to secure Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior fall through this summer, with them choosing to sign for Chelsea and stay at Real Madrid respectively.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'prepare bid' for £51m Brighton star amid Man Utd and Man City competition
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'prepare bid' for £51m Brighton star amid Man Utd and Man City competition

Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City are all weighing up whether to move for Brighton midfielder Jack Hinshelwood, who is valued at £51million by his club

View 2 Images Jack Hinshelwood is attracting transfer interest (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Arsenal are reportedly ready to challenge Manchester United and Manchester City for Brighton star Jack Hinshelwood. The 21-year-old midfielder has caught the eye of Arsenal's scouting department and the club are said to be readying an official bid.

‌



Hinshelwood is an England under-21 international who already has a great deal of Premier League experience, having made 79 appearances for Brighton, with 12 goals and seven assists to his name.

‌



His versatility is a real selling point: he is capable of playing across midfielder or in both full-back positions. That is particularly attractive to Mikel Arteta, who is known to favour players who can offer him tactical flexibility.

‌



Brighton have proven to be shrewd negotiators in recent years and reportedly value their academy graduate around the £43m to £51m mark. The Sun reports that United have longstanding interest in Hinshelwood while City are also weighing up a move.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

United have already enquired about Hinshelwood's availability and are planning their own offer. He is under contract with Brighton until June 2029 and the multiple interested parties could help the Seagulls drive up the price.

‌



Arsenal have already spent £75m to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, but remain keen to add further depth to their squad. United, meanwhile, have brought in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos for a combined £85m, yet Michael Carrick wants another central midfielder for his squad.

Arteta has been very open about the need for more arrivals this summer, with Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis the only major additions so far. “There is more that we want to do, because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that,” he said this week.

View 2 Images Jack Hinshelwood has lots of Premier League experience (Image: David Horton/Getty Images)

‌



“We’re actively trying to do so – the thing is, in the market, it doesn’t just depend on you, and we’re very clear on that. The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we’re going to do it because it doesn’t only depend on us.”

Carrick has been similarly forthright in his words, with United going over a month since their last signing. A left-back to provide competition for Luke Shaw is the other area of interest along with midfield.

"I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more," he said.

‌

That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious."

Sports.title: UFC 330 Islam Makhachev vs Ian Garry start time and how to watch tonight
Sports.content:
UFC 330 Islam Makhachev vs Ian Garry start time and how to watch tonight

Islam Makhachev puts his welterweight title on the line tonight when he takes on Ireland's Ian Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia

View Image Islam Makhachev takes on Ian Machado Garry

Ian Machado Garry will attempt to dethrone one of the best fighters in UFC history tonight when he takes on welterweight world champion Islam Makhachev.

‌



Makhachev himself is attempting to create history by winning a 15th successive fight in the promotion, which would take him clear of Anderson Silva's long-standing record. Makhachev, who has Khabib Nurmagomedov as his coach, won the 170lb belt last year when he dethroned Jack Della Maddalena.

‌



Machado Garry has only fought twice since he lost for the first time against Shavkat Rakhmonov two years ago. Victories over Carlos Prates and Belal Muhammad have catapulted him into a title shot. Also on the card, women's strawweight world champion Mackenzie Dern defends her belt against Gillian Robertson. Here is everything you need to know about tonight's fights...

‌



What UK time is UFC 330 Makhachev vs Garry?

Islam Makhachev and Ian Garry will fight at around 5am UK time. The main card, which consists of five fights - including two five-round title fights - will kick off at 2am. All fight times are subject to change depending on how long the earlier bouts take to complete.

How to watch and stream UFC 330 Makhachev vs Garry

UFC 330 will be shown live on TNT Sports in the UK. The prelim fights will be shown from midnight before the main event starts at 2am on Sunday morning. The streaming home for TNT Sports in the UK is HBO Max, where fans can enjoy a subscription that includes TNT Sports and entertainment in one destination. Sports.title: Formula E was a child, now it's a teenager and needs more space, says CEO
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Formula E was a child, now it's a teenager and needs more space, says CEO

Jeff Dodds believes that the new power and speed of the Formula E car is the key behind the growth of the sport from street circuits to world renowned racetracks

View 2 Images Formula E is moving away from the novelties (Image: Getty Images)

Formula E is finally growing up, says CEO Jeff Dodds. The all-electric series' entertainment extravaganza at London's ExCeL Centre will be unplugged for the final time today - but only to make way for bigger things at Brands Hatch next season.

‌



The fourth generation of FE car comes out of the garage later this year and it is now too fast and too powerful for the majority of the city centre street circuits on which the series was built. It marks a significant shift as the sport brushes off concerns it is a novelty, to prove its technology is actually the future.

‌



Dodds, the ex-Virgin chief who took over the series in 2023, says: "If you took the Gen4 car and transported it back in time, I don't think you could put it on any race track that we raced on in Gen1, because it's too big, too powerful, too fast accelerating. It was a child 12 years ago and needed certain things. It's now a teenager and it needs different things. It's just grown up.

‌



"Yes, Formula E might have lost some of its identity, but it's developed a different identity; one that can get to 100 kilometres an hour in about 1.7 or 1.8 seconds. It's doing different things today."

Five different F1 drivers, including Lando Norris, turned up to the Monaco E-Prix earlier this year - and the new Gen4 car only got positive reviews.

"We've got a lot of drivers there saying nice things, saying this is a beast of a car and people are excited to see it in action," says Dodds. "Of course my ears prick up when I hear that, because I'm like a proud dad. When I hear them say nice things about my child, it makes me feel good."

‌



This weekend's London E-Prix is the final tango for the ExCeL Centre. The world's only half-indoor, half-outdoor world championship racing circuit, the unique nature of the venue meant that it has been a perfect home for entertainment to cross over with sport.

View 2 Images Jeff Dodds has seen the FE car's capability grow significantly in recent years (Image: LAT Images)

FE's London race will move to the historic Brands Hatch from next summer - but Dodds says that entertainment will still be the order of the day.

‌



"We'll still expect to have music and entertainment, loads of stuff for families to come and do," he says. "It's obviously within proximity of London. But the differences will be that it's a big old racetrack.

"You're going to see the full Grand Prix circuit, and you're going to see those cars spinning around at maximum speed. And if you know the circuit, you can sit at the top and look at about 60% of the race.

"I think you're going to get a lot of people at Brands Hatch, but we're going to try and retain some of that entertainment around the show. It will be a pure motorsport event with a load of entertainment to make it feel more like Formula E.

Article continues below

"We can do our thing and respect the history of the circuit, but we don't have to do what's happened on the circuit, we can bring our own personality to it.

"You want to nod to the past. We want to respect that, in the same way as Monaco. They've been racing for 93 years on that circuit, the street circuit, but when we show up we have 200 overtakes, we put on our own show, it's got a load of people come to watch it."

Sports.title: 'I was the next Lionel Messi – now I'm making music after tough times on the pitch'
Sports.content:
'I was the next Lionel Messi – now I'm making music after tough times on the pitch'

The former Barcelona star turned to making music as a way of dealing with a hard period in his life

View 3 Images Ansu Fati was pnce viewed as Lionel Messi's successor (Image: Alex Caparros, Getty Images)

Being dubbed the next Lionel Messi is quite the burden. And for Ansu Fati, the former Barcelona prodigy now playing for Monaco, it hasn't worked out as hoped.

‌



The 23-year-old is looking to reignite his career in Ligue 1 after signing for the French side this summer following a successful loan period there last term. Fati has also turned to music as a form of therapy to help him navigate rocky periods and the expectation that came with his bursting onto the scene in 2019.

‌



At just 16 years and 318 days old, he became the youngest player this century to score and assist in the same La Liga fixture. Such was he a beacon of Barcelona's future, he was even given the No. 10 jersey after Messi's departure in 2021.

‌



Fati's promising career was blighted with injuries, however, including a meniscus tear in 2020 that kept him out for nine months. Consistent muscle problems followed. To jolt his career back to life he even joined Brighton on loan, getting a brief taste of the Premier League in the 2023/2024 campaign, where he managed four goals in 27 games.

And so music it is, as he attempts to anchor himself back to happiness. The attacking star has released a track titled Sea Como Sea" The song’s name means 'Whatever It Takes' and it has racked up a staggering 1.1million views on YouTube.

Fati said: “Singing is a hobby. I’ve always loved music, and people who know me know it’s something I’ve had since I was a child. But football is my passion, and I can’t compare it to anything, I have several songs I’m working on, and the idea is to release them soon.

“Sometimes when you’re alone, you just start writing and they just came out. I had some tough periods where it helped me get out of that rut.”

On the meaning of the song, he said: “A lot of people ask me if this song Sea Como Sea is about a girl or what. I’m not going to say. It’s a concept – everyone can interpret it as they feel it, as they feel at that moment. But basically it’s that with hard work and dedication you can achieve whatever you want, no matter what.”

He has fans in high places, too. Another Barcelona heir to Messi's throne, World Cup winner Lamine Yamal, is one. Fati added: “They weren’t surprised because I’ve always been one of those who plays music in the locker room or is always singing and dancing.

‌



"I shared them with several people, like Gavi, Lamine, [Alejandro] Balde, [Ronald] Araujo. They also gave me a big push, telling me to release it because people would like it. It would be a dream to one day be able to sing in front of so many people and show them my songs.”

Fati won two La Liga titles, two Copa del Rey titles and one Spanish Super Cup with the Catalan giants. Monaco forked out £9.3m for the player who scored 29 goals for Barcelona and once had a €1billion release clause.

I spent many years at Barça and left behind friends and people from La Masia (Barcelona's training facility). The first few days were sad, but that's life. You have to accept what comes and keep looking forward."

As of yet, Fati has not played a single minute of Monaco's pre-season, as his new permanent side looks to get him in shape ahead of their opening Ligue 1 clash with La Havre on Sunday, August 23. But after scoring 12 times for the French side last season, he looks to be on the right path.

Sports.title: 11 transfers that managers didn't want – but the club signed them anyway
Sports.content:
11 transfers that managers didn't want – but the club signed them anyway

Sometimes a manager is against a signing but the club still goes ahead and completes the deal - and it happens more often than one might think

View 11 Images Paul Pogba's blockbuster Manchester United move is one example where the manager was left irked (Image: Getty)

Transfers aren't always as straightforward as most of this summer window's moves have been. With less than a week left until the start of the new Premier League season, we've seen records broken and allegiances shifting left, right and centre.

‌



Morgan Rogers became the most expensive British player in history when he completed his £117million switch to Chelsea last month, following in international team-mate Elliot Anderson's footsteps after he swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City in a deal worth £116m.

‌



The window has been a relatively dramatic one with other stars like former Newcastle United trio Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon all changing hands for sizable fees, and more moves are on the cards too as clubs reinforce ahead of the new campaign and the September 1 deadline day.

‌



But with all those transfers, it's highly likely the club's managers either sanctioned the purchases or will at least be overjoyed to welcome new faces to their squads. This isn't always the case. Mirror Football takes a look back at instances where a transfer wasn't the manager's decision, but the club still went ahead with the deal.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival READ MORE :

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee

When Manchester United purchased Joshua Zirkzee from Italian side Bologna in 2024 for £36.5million, he became the first signing of the INEOS era at Old Trafford. Then-manager Erik ten Hag was given a new promising striker to work with. But the only issue? He'd requested a different type of forward.

‌



View 11 Images Zirkzee has flopped at United (Image: Getty)

Not long after Zirkzee's arrival, the under-pressure Ten Hag was relieved of his duties after a dismal start to the season and was replaced by Ruben Amorim. After his dismissal, reports broke suggesting that the Dutch boss was frustrated at the Zirkzee signing, as it was driven by INEOS, to whom he had requested a proven Premier League striker.

Zirkzee could do nothing to save Ten Hag's job and even under Amorim, he barely showed glimpses of the talent that shone in Italy. He could leave the club this summer, with Amorim supplanted by Michael Carrick. Zirkzee started just five games last term.

‌



Djed Spence

Tottenham defender Djed Spence was one of World Cup 2026's brightest lights and he made his mark in an England side that fell at the semi-final stage. But his path to becoming a Three Lions hero was not a straightforward one.

In 2022, Spence was snapped up by Spurs for £20m from Middlesbrough, having impressed the season prior on loan at Nottingham Forest. Antonio Conte was the manager at the time and he sensationally admitted that the full-back wasn't his signing, it was the club's.

View 11 Images Spence was not wanted by Conte (Image: Getty)

‌



"Spence is an investment of the club," said Conte. "The club wanted to do it. I said OK, this player is young but he showed he can become a good, important player for us. The club decided to buy him."

Under Conte, Spence played sparingly and in January 2023 he was sent out on loan to Rennes. In the summer, he joined Leeds United, but this loan was cut short. Genoa took him on for the second half of the 2023/24 campaign. These moves somehow paid off as the 2024/25 campaign was a breakout one and he played admirably last season before earning a World Cup call-up.

Paul Pogba

There was barely a United supporter alive who wasn't thrilled at the prospect of bringing Paul Pogba back from Juventus in 2016 — yet Jose Mourinho wasn't quite so enthused.

‌



View 11 Images Pogba was an expensive buy (Image: Getty)

At least, that's according to Mourinho's close friend and former adviser Eladio Parames, who lifted the lid in 2018 on what went on behind the scenes as 'The Special One' looked to stamp his authority.

"Sometimes there are reasons beyond sports that lead the clubs, and not always the coaches, to gamble on hiring players," he told Record at the time. "Pogba, for example, is worth a lot in the advertising market, so much so that in just six months Manchester United had already recovered what they had invested in him [£89million].

‌



"However, without terriers like Blaise Matuidi and N'Golo Kante at his side, he is worth ­virtually nothing on the field. United did not give Mourinho terriers despite advice given to Ed Woodward last summer."

Olivier Ntcham

Marseille's decision to bring in Celtic playmaker Olivier Ntcham proved such a bitter pill to swallow for Andre Villas-Boas that it ultimately cost him his job.

View 11 Images Ntcham is a former Celtic star (Image: Getty)

‌



The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager not only walked away from his role at the Velodrome following Ntcham's loan arrival in February 2021, but sensationally quit management for good.

"I have resigned because I don't agree with the sporting policy of the club," Villas-Boas told reporters in 2021. "I said no to the signing of Olivier Ntcham. He wasn't on our list. I had nothing to do with this decision. Ntcham is a player I said no to. I was not aware [he had signed], I learned it in the press this morning when I woke up."

Joelinton

Newcastle fans would have been forgiven for considering Joelinton a waste of money following his £40m switch from Hoffenheim in 2019. Former Magpies owner Mike Ashley once disclosed that Rafa Benitez was among those unconvinced about sanctioning the transfer in the first place.

‌



View 11 Images Joelinton went on to become a Magpies fan favourite (Image: Getty)

"He thought the £40m for Joelinton wasn't worth it. It's too much and the club shouldn't spend it," Ashley told the Daily Mail in 2019. "Very occasionally, I get to be me in this world. So here's the deal. I'll pay £20m of it personally. Nothing to do with the club. Above and beyond the budget.

"Rafa valued him at £20m. So that's what would come out of the club budget. The rest, £23m – I'll pay. And he still didn't sign it off. Looking back, I think he knew for a long time he was going to China because it was like we couldn't do anything. Joelinton was the test."

‌

Winston Bogarde

Chelsea's haphazard approach to recruitment is still a topic of discussion. Yet, any contemporary chaos would struggle to rival the shambolic scenes witnessed at the turn of the millennium when an ageing Winston Bogarde rocked up from Barcelona.

Reports at the time suggested that then-manager Gianluca Vialli had been kept in the dark over the transfer, with director Colin Hutchinson having actually overseen the deal.

‌



View 11 Images Bogarde's transfer was kept a secret from the manager (Image: Getty)

The late Vialli was dismissed by Chelsea shortly after Bogarde's arrival and he rounded off his four-year stint at Stamford Bridge as a notorious flop after Claudio Ranieri showed no interest whatsoever in the defender.

"You may have seen reports in the press that Vialli never wanted to sign me in the first place and it was my arrival that quickened his departure," said Bogarde following Vialli's exit. "As far as I am concerned, I was not aware of any of this."

‌



Andriy Shevchenko

A 29-year-old Andriy Shevchenko ought to have been music to the ears of virtually any manager, but then Mourinho was never your typical boss.

Having netted 173 goals in 296 appearances for AC Milan, Ukrainian legend Shevchenko was brought to west London by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich, yet managed just 23 goals during a dismal two-season stint at Chelsea.

View 11 Images Shevchenko is a Ballon d'Or winner (Image: Getty)

‌



"He was like a prince in Milan and at Chelsea our philosophy was different, we had no princes," said Mourinho upon leaving the club in 2007. "Everybody needs to work like everybody else and everybody needs to prove he deserves to play. I think maybe he lost some self-confidence. Step by step a player goes in the wrong direction. He was not my first option."

Mario Balotelli

For all the indications that Brendan Rodgers enjoyed ultimate authority over Liverpool's transfer activity during his Anfield tenure, Mario Balotelli is one acquisition he's sought to distance himself from.

Stepping into Luis Suarez's shoes in 2014 proved a daunting challenge, but the Reds eventually settled on former Man City striker Balotelli as their solution - though Rodgers hardly wanted his arrival.

‌



View 11 Images Balotelli's Liverpool stint was short-lived (Image: Getty)

"What we wanted and what we needed was a player who could really press at the top end of the field. It wasn't just a goalscorer we were after," the Northern Irishman subsequently admitted in 2016. "I felt Mario was someone who wouldn't work for us. But come the end of the summer, we were struggling to get someone who could do the role we wanted."

Xisco and Ignacio Gonzalez

The late Kevin Keegan's second stint as Newcastle boss was not one to remember. Matters reached a breaking point following the 2008 summer transfer window, when the manager learnt that the Spaniard Xisco and the Uruguayan Ignacio Gonzalez were being imposed upon him.

‌



View 11 Images Xisco's arrival didn't please Keegan (Image: Getty)

Keegan wrote in his 2018 autobiography, My Life In Football: "It wasn't Mike's beer-guzzling that upset me that day. It was the fact that Tony Jimenez, the executive who had been put in charge of Newcastle's transfer business, had informed me we were spending £5.7m on a Spanish player called Xisco whom nobody from the club had ever seen play.

"On the same day the Xisco bombshell was dropped, I had also found out a Uruguayan by the name of Ignacio Gonzalez was joining us as a 'favour' for two South American agents.

‌



"When I rang Dennis [Wise] to explain it was out of the question, he seemed determined to change my mind. Gonzalez, he said, was a 'great player,' and our contacts in South America meant we had the chance to get him on a season-long loan. He was adamant we should give him a go and suggested that if I clicked on YouTube I might find some footage to change my opinion."

Timo Werner

Frank Lampard faced no shortage of obstacles during his first spell as Chelsea boss, not least the fact that he had little say over incoming transfers.

That power rested primarily with former director Marina Granovskaia and The Athletic reported that the fractured relationship between the pair played a significant role in Lampard's eventual departure from the club.

Article continues below

View 11 Images Lampard didn't request Werner's transfer (Image: Getty)

One such signing Lampard reportedly never requested - or at least not at that particular time - was RB Leipzig striker Timo Werner. Arriving in the summer of 2020, Lampard had previously lobbied for the Blues to bring in Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang that January, but was instead left with an alternative who failed to live up to expectations in west London.

"The two German players [Kai Havertz and Werner] have been massive disappointments, massive," said Harry Redknapp of his nephew's signings that summer. "I'm not even sure Timo Werner is cut out for Premier League football, the physical side is too much for him. I doubt very much whether Frank had a big say over in who came in."

Sports.title: 'I played golf against Donald Trump – he's exactly what you think he's like'
Sports.content:
'I played golf against Donald Trump – he's exactly what you think he's like'

Donald Trump recently faced social media backlash questioning his golf victory and one star who played with him has revealed his true nature

View 2 Images US president Donald Trump's behaviour on the golf course has been scrutinised (Image: Getty)

PGA Tour golfer Sam Burns once claimed Donald Trump is exactly as one would expect on the golf course, highlighting his "brutal honesty". Yet, the United States president was recently the subject of new accusations of cheating after his latest victory.

‌



Trump, who is presently serving his second presidential term, is known for being passionate about golf. The billionaire businessman has even faced claims of displaying greater commitment to his hobby than his presidency, with reports in 2025 claiming that he had spent roughly 25 per cent of his days in office visiting golf courses.

‌



The 80-year-old also owns numerous courses throughout the US, Europe and Asia. It was at one of these venues - Trump National Bedminster in New Jersey - that he clinched his latest success in the Bedminster Club Championship earlier this month.

‌



Trump took to his social media platform, Truth Social, to claim he had secured victories in both the senior and super senior categories with a score of 70, and posted a clip of his winning shot.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gianni Infantino cornered as three federations pile pressure on under-fire FIFA boss READ MORE :

He wrote: "I won with a score of 70, and am so honoured in that, unlike the rest of the field, I'm given very little time to practice, because I'm focused on many other things. It's called TALENT, and I have it, and they don't!"

‌



But not everyone believed that the politician genuinely recorded a two under par round. Golf enthusiasts flocked to social media to suggest impropriety, with one fan claiming: "Watched him live for years, listened to his caddie's stories. Everyone around him allows him to cheat out of fear. Nothing he does is genuine. All his 'feats' are fake, and he actually feels special."

Another alleged to have witnessed footage of the president's caddie repositioning the ball for him. On a video posted by Trump of him executing the 'winning shot' at the Bedminster Club Championship, more users questioned the footage, which showed a ball delicately chipped onto the green and rolling to a stop near the hole.
